Emit, and Let Listeners React →

Side Effects Piling Up

What createTicket would look like if it did all of a notification's work itself — and why that's a service that keeps changing for the wrong reasons.

Creating a ticket, from Week 3, is one Prisma call: prisma.ticket.create(...). But the planning brief's domain events list a lot more that's supposed to happen the moment a ticket exists — a confirmation email to the customer, an in-app notification for every agent, a live update if one happens to be online. If none of that lived anywhere else, it would all have to be written directly into createTicket itself:

// Not real code — the shape createTicket would have if it did everything
// itself, with nowhere else for any of this to live.
export const createTicket = async ({ subject, description, customerId }) => {
  const ticket = await prisma.ticket.create({ data: { subject, description, customerId }, include: { customer: true } });

  await mailer.sendMail({ to: ticket.customer.email, subject: `Ticket #${ticket.id} created`, text: '...' });

  const agents = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { role: 'agent' } });
  await prisma.notification.createMany({ data: agents.map((a) => ({ userId: a.id, message: '...' })) });

  getIO().to('role:agent').emit('ticket.created', ticket);

  return ticket;
};

Nothing about this is wrong, exactly — it would work. But look at what createTicket now has to know about: how to send an email, which users count as "the agent queue," the shape of a Notification row, and a Socket.IO room naming scheme. A function whose actual job is "insert a ticket row" now has four unrelated jobs, and every one of them is a reason it might need to change later — a fifth notification channel, a change to who counts as an agent, a different email template — none of which have anything to do with creating a ticket.

It gets worse the moment a second place needs the same reaction. ticket.commented notifies watchers; ticket.status_changed notifies the customer again — each would repeat its own copy of "email, in-app row, socket push," maybe not quite consistently, maybe missing one channel because whoever wrote that path forgot it. The problem isn't any one line above — it's that triggering a reaction and carrying it out have been welded into the same function, with no way to change one without touching the other.
